Hi Oliver / Marissa —

Thanks — quick technical/legal responses below to help you and Acme Legal: 

1) SOC 2: the attached Redwood_SOC2_Report_RTA.pdf is the Type II report for the period ending 2025-12-31; we also have a SOC 2 Type II bridge letter for 2026 coverage that we can provide under an NDA. We will coordinate with our auditors to provide the bridge letter that references controls continuity through Sep 30, 2026.

2) SCCs / Controller-Processor: Redwood is the processor for the hosting and inference service. Standard recommendation for EU controller -> processor transfers is SCC Module 2 (controller to processor) in combination with the Redwood subprocessors addendum. For large enterprise customers that require more granular controls we also offer Module 3 mapping; I'll attach a CSV with the typical mapping.

3) Data residency / logs: by default analytics/monitoring logs are stored in the region where the customer's instance is deployed. For the Acme pilot we can restrict logs/analytics to US-only region for the accounts in scope; retention defaults are 90 days for debug logs and 365 days for audit logs, but retention can be shortened via contract.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), SCC_Annex_Options.csv (text/csv)

Next steps: we can send the DPA draft with Module 2 pre-selected and call out Module 3 as an optional add-on. If Acme Legal prefers DocuSign routing, we're good with that.

Happy to jump on a short call with Acme Legal to walk through the DPA/SCC mapping if helpful.

Best,
